findings.title: Prepared config copy is discarded; raw monitor config is sent in the monitor context
findings.body: `get_monitor_environment_context` copies `monitor.config` and replaces `schedule_type` with its human-readable display value. The returned dict then uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` instead of the local `config`, so that copy is never used. As a result, the `monitor` context on every issue occurrence carries the raw integer `schedule_type` rather than the display name. The bug was carried over from mark_failed.py, but the function now lives in a new module. Fix: return `"config": config`.

findings.title: Moved helpers removed from mark_failed without re-exports or test updates
findings.body:
Several names were removed from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`:
- `mark_failed_threshold`, renamed to `try_incident_threshold`
- `create_issue_platform_occurrence`, renamed to `create_incident_occurrence`
- `get_failure_reason`
- `get_monitor_environment_context`
- `SimpleCheckIn`

No compatibility re-exports were added, and no tests were updated in this PR. Any code or tests that import these names from `mark_failed`, or use them as `mock.patch` targets, will fail with ImportError/AttributeError. Either update those references and the tests in the same change, or keep temporary aliases.

findings.title: get_failure_reason docstring examples don't match actual output
findings.body:
The docstring has typos ("humam readible") and its examples don't match the code.
- It claims output like "2 missed check-ins, 1 timeout check-in and 1 error check-in were detected". The code actually produces "2 missed, 1 timeout and 1 error check-ins detected".
- It claims "A failed check-in was detected". No such string exists in `SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP`; the singular forms are status-specific ("A missed check-in was detected", etc.).

The docstring is now in a fresh module and should describe the real behavior.
